memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If you put all these people to death, leaving none alive, the nations who have heard this report about you will say, 'The Lord was not able to bring these people into the land he promised them on oath, so he slaughtered them in the wilderness.' Now may the Lord's strength be displayed, just as you have declared: 'The Lord is slow to anger, abounding in love and forgiving sin and rebellion. Yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished; he punishes the children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation.'" — Num 14:15-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses continues his plea, and now he reaches for the very words God had spoken about Himself. He quotes God back to God: "The Lord is slow to anger, abounding in love and forgiving sin and rebellion." This is the most powerful kind of prayer — asking God to act in keeping with His own revealed character.

There is a beautiful lesson here about how to pray. Moses does not appeal to Israel's worthiness, for they had none. He appeals to God's nature — His patience, His steadfast love, His readiness to forgive. When we come to God, we too come not on the basis of our goodness but on the basis of His. We can pray, "Lord, You are merciful; act toward me according to Your mercy."

Notice that Moses does not ignore God's justice. He quotes the whole truth: God is loving and forgiving, "yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished." Moses holds together God's mercy and His justice, not playing one against the other. God's love never cancels His holiness; both are fully real.

This tension finds its resolution only at the cross. There, God's steadfast love and His justice meet perfectly. Sin is not swept under the rug — it is fully punished in Christ, who bore what we deserved. And mercy flows freely — because the guilt has been paid. When you pray for forgiveness, you stand on firmer ground than Moses ever did: not merely on God's character in the abstract, but on the finished work of His Son.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you pray on the basis of your own worthiness or God's character?
2. How do you hold together God's mercy and His justice in your thinking?
3. How does the cross show both fully satisfied at once?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are slow to anger and abounding in love, yet perfectly just. Teach me to pray on the basis of who You are. Thank You that at the cross Your mercy and justice meet in Christ. Amen.
